text: Owner decision 2026-07-21: the logical-map Artifact mirror (claude.ai/code/artifact/f20dda86-f0ac-4dba-b2a1-a191e6c3b034) is RETIRED — never republish it after map changes. Fully redundant with the permanent public Pages URL, and each republish costs an unavoidable web permission prompt (claude.ai web sessions apply no permission allowlists). The map's only maintained home is docs/site/logical-map.html served via Pages.

Owner decision 2026-07-21: docs/site/repo-map.html (physical-folders view) is deleted; docs/site/logical-map.html is the repo's single map. The add-a-file inventory drill now touches ONE map (SELF frame counts + Σ), CLAUDE.md layout table, and this file. Legacy stub docs/repo-map.html redirects to the logical map.

GitHub REST and GraphQL are separate quota pools drawn by every session on the account. Merging is REST; leaving draft is GraphQL-only, so a GraphQL-exhausted session can merge a non-draft PR but not un-draft one. Un-draft as soon as CI is green. Diagnose from the failing verb, and treat a throttle as retryable, never as a broken repo.

A UI suite written from the implementation confirms the implementation. Name the observable outcome first, then assert against it: 'the legend opens', not 'the handler fires'. Proven 2026-08-01 on this repo's map, where a 27-assertion Playwright gate stayed green through four interaction bugs a human found in minutes.

REJECTED: changing the PR-draft default to open ready-for-review. Raised after an exhausted GraphQL pool stalled three green PRs at un-draft. The cause was session volume, not the draft policy, and git.md's existing mitigation already covers it — un-draft as soon as CI goes green. Opening ready-for-review stays a per-PR judgement when already quota-strained.

Creating a PR subscribes the session to its activity harness-side; no tool call is involved and omitting one prevents nothing. subscribe_pr_activity exists to take over a PR the session did not open, or to re-subscribe after unsubscribing. The only lever on your own PR is unsubscribe_pr_activity after the fact.

Never judge Codex from the codex-flagged label: written asynchronously, so absence proves nothing though presence still blocks. Match reviews and clean comments to HEAD by SHA and verify Codex authored them; a bare 👍 has no SHA, so accept it only when its review request postdates the push. Read inline comments; if that GraphQL call fails, the gate is uncleared.

A skipped-test CI gate cannot key on whether a skip carries a reason string: every shipped test.skip has one, including the fixture-absence skips it must catch. Key an allowlist by stable test identity — project, spec file, full test title — checked against a JSON reporter run, so intended skips are enumerated once and any new skip fails.

One shared environment serves every repo, and its cached image keeps whatever plugins the installer once installed. Re-saving the Setup script does not reliably rebuild it. So an installer fix reaches only repos that commit .claude/hooks/session-start.sh. Symptom: one repo spews a plugin error while claude.directives is clean — the difference is the hook, not the environment.

The owner dislikes the <wake reason=...> event-envelope messages in session transcripts and has asked twice (2026-08-20) to stop them appearing - treat as decided. The envelope rendering is platform-side and no repo config suppresses it, so the rule is to make wakes rare: while the owner is actively watching a session, do NOT rely on PR event subscriptions (each comment/review/CI event is one envelope) - unsubscribe right after opening a PR and collapse the whole watched operation into ONE scheduled check-in that verifies CI, merges, and cleans up in a single wake. Delete drained triggers immediately; batch work so one wake carries several results. Unattended/overnight sessions may still use subscriptions; the Status Line heartbeat ruling stands where it applies.
